title: Elementary charge and charges of particles
body: The elementary charge e is the magnitude of the charge of a single electron or proton and is the smallest indivisible amount of charge; an electron has charge −e, a proton has charge +e, and a neutron has no charge.
ced_evidence: 8.1.A.1.ii–iii: "The charge of an electron is −e and the charge of a proton is +e, and a neutron has no electric charge."

title: Charge as a scalar
body: Charge is a scalar quantity described as positive or negative, so its sign (not a direction) determines whether forces are attractive or repulsive.
ced_evidence: 8.1.A.1.i: "Charge is a scalar quantity and is described as positive or negative."

title: Limit on discrete-charge force calculations
body: Calculate the electric force on charges only for four or fewer interacting charged objects or systems, unless the situation has high symmetry.
ced_evidence: Topic 8.1 Boundary Statement: "only expects students to make calculations of the electric force between four or fewer interacting charged objects or systems"

title: Electric permittivity
body: Electric permittivity is a measure of the degree to which a material or medium is polarized in the presence of an electric field; free space has a constant permittivity \epsilon_0, and matter's permittivity differs from it because of the matter's composition and arrangement.
ced_evidence: 8.1.C.1: "Electric permittivity is a measurement of the degree to which a material or medium is polarized in the presence of an electric field."; 8.1.C.3; 8.1.C.4

title: Electric polarization
body: Electric polarization is modeled as the induced rearrangement of electrons by an external electric field, resulting in a separation of positive and negative charges within a material or medium.
ced_evidence: 8.1.C.2: "induced rearrangement of electrons by an external electric field, resulting in a separation of positive and negative charges"; 8.2.A.1.ii

title: Conductor in electrostatic equilibrium
body: In electrostatic equilibrium, the excess charge of a conductor lies on its surface, the electric field within the conductor is zero, and the field at the surface is perpendicular to the surface.
caution: Zero field inside applies to a conductor in electrostatic equilibrium, not to insulators.
ced_evidence: 8.3.B.1 and 8.3.B.1.i: "the excess charge of a conductor is distributed on the surface of the conductor, and the electric field within the conductor is zero"

title: Field outside a spherically symmetric charge
body: The electric field outside an isolated sphere with spherically symmetric charge distribution is the same as that of a point charge with the sphere's net charge located at its center.
caution: This applies outside the sphere; it does not describe the field inside the sphere.
ced_evidence: 8.3.B.1.ii: "the same as the electric field due to a point charge with the same net charge as the sphere located at the center of the sphere"

title: Insulator in electrostatic equilibrium
body: In electrostatic equilibrium, the excess charge of an insulator is distributed throughout its interior as well as at its surface, and the electric field within the insulator may be nonzero.
ced_evidence: 8.3.B.2: "the excess charge of an insulator is distributed throughout the interior of the insulator as well as at the surface"
